title: Knowledge check: Request Parsing and Response Construction

questions.prompt: Which backend structure keeps a REST API maintainable?
options: Put SQL, authorization, business rules, serialization, and retries into one route handler.
Make business rules depend on the browser’s current UI state.
Use global mutable state as the only communication path between all layers.
Separate transport/routing from use cases, domain rules, and persistence; inject boundaries so behavior can be tested.
questions.answer_key: Separate transport/routing from use cases, domain rules, and persistence; inject boundaries so behavior can be tested.
questions.explanation: Separate transport/routing from use cases, domain rules, and persistence; inject boundaries so behavior can be tested. This is especially relevant to “Request Parsing and Response Construction” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Request Parsing and Response Construction”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Test use-case logic separately, then verify its integration with routing and persistence.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
questions.answer_key: Test use-case logic separately, then verify its integration with routing and persistence.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Request Parsing and Response Construction”?
options: The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
Controllers contain persistence, business logic, and external-service behavior in one untestable block.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
questions.answer_key: Controllers contain persistence, business logic, and external-service behavior in one untestable block.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
